category: CFD Module: Turbulence Models, LES/DES, High Mach Number and Potential Flow
description: Single-phase CFD interfaces of the COMSOL CFD Module beyond laminar flow: every RANS eddy-viscosity and Reynolds-stress turbulence model, large and detached eddy simulation, high Mach number (compressible, transonic and supersonic) flow, the time-explicit compressible Euler solver and incompressible potential flow, with their key settings and verified Java type strings (COMSOL 6.4).

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, Algebraic yPlus (spf)
tools.description: RANS interface whose eddy viscosity is computed from an algebraic expression of the local scaled wall distance (y+) instead of extra transport equations, so it only solves the RANS equations plus a wall distance equation. It is very robust and cheap and is the usual choice for internal flows such as electronics cooling, HVAC ducts and mixers where a first turbulent estimate is needed. Automatic wall treatment (low-Re near resolved walls, wall functions elsewhere) is the default.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, Algebraic yPlus (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowAlgebraicYplus", "geom1")

parameters.name: Turbulence model type / Turbulence model
parameters.description: prop("TurbulenceModelProperty") TurbulenceModelType=RANS and TurbulenceModel=AlgebraicYplus; switch to another RANS model without recreating the interface.

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: WallTreatment = Automatic (default) or LowReynoldsNumber.

parameters.name: Enable porous media domains
parameters.description: Adds Fluid and Matrix Properties, Mass Source and Forchheimer Drag to model turbulent flow through porous regions.

parameters.name: Wall Distance Initialization
parameters.description: The study needs a Wall Distance Initialization step before Stationary/Time Dependent.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (also in the Heat Transfer Module). Good initial guess for k-ε/SST runs via Generate New Turbulence Model Interface. Accuracy for separated or strongly rotating flows is limited.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, L-VEL (spf)
tools.description: Algebraic RANS model that derives the eddy viscosity from the local wall distance and a local velocity scale (the L-VEL formulation), again solving only the RANS equations plus a wall distance equation. It is more accurate than Algebraic yPlus for internal flows while staying almost as robust, and is widely used for electronic enclosures and ventilation where many small channels exist. Default wall treatment is Automatic.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, L-VEL (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowLVEL", "geom1")

parameters.name: TurbulenceModel
parameters.description: LVEL in prop("TurbulenceModelProperty"); model constants kappaL and Elvel are editable.

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Automatic (default) or Low Re.

parameters.name: Enable porous media domains
parameters.description: Couples turbulent free flow with Brinkman-type porous regions.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module or Heat Transfer Module. Not suited for external aerodynamics or free shear layers far from walls; use k-ε/SST there.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, Realizable k-ε (spf)
tools.description: Two-equation realizable k-epsilon model in which C_mu varies with strain and rotation so that normal Reynolds stresses stay positive; it improves predictions for jets, swirling flows, separation and recirculation compared with the standard k-ε model. Near walls it uses wall functions like standard k-ε. Optional rotation-curvature correction modifies the production terms for rotating or strongly curved flows.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, Realizable k-ε (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowRealizablekeps", "geom1")

parameters.name: TurbulenceModel
parameters.description: Rkeps in prop("TurbulenceModelProperty").

parameters.name: includeRotationCurvatureCorrection
parameters.description: 1 to multiply k and ε production by a rotation/curvature factor (accounts for Frozen Rotor or Rotating Frame rotation).

parameters.name: Edit turbulence model parameters
parameters.description: C2 (RkepsC2), A0, sigma_k, sigma_eps_Rkeps, kappa_v, B.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Wall functions require y+ (spf.Delta_wPlus on walls) around 11.06 or more; refine the boundary layer mesh accordingly.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, Low Re k-ε (spf)
tools.description: AKN low-Reynolds-number k-epsilon model with realizability constraints that can resolve the boundary layer all the way to the wall; it therefore includes a wall distance equation. It gives better wall shear stress and heat transfer than wall-function k-ε for attached and mildly separated flows and handles adjacent free/porous regions well. Automatic wall treatment is default; Low Re enforces full resolution.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, Low Re k-ε (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowlowRekeps", "geom1")

parameters.name: TurbulenceModel
parameters.description: lowRekeps; constants lowReCeps1, lowReCeps2, lowResigmak, lowResigmaeps.

parameters.name: WallTreatment
parameters.description: Automatic (default) or LowReynoldsNumber (needs y+ about 1).

parameters.name: includeRotationCurvatureCorrection
parameters.description: Optional rotation-curvature correction.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Note the Java id uses lowercase 'low': TurbulentFlowlowRekeps (the High Mach variant is HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentLowRekeps).

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, v2-f (spf)
tools.description: Four-equation v2-f model (k, ε, turbulent relative fluctuations ζ and elliptic relaxation α) that accounts for near-wall anisotropy and blocking effects while remaining an eddy-viscosity model. It resolves the flow down to the wall and performs well for swirling flows, impingement and heat transfer where k-ε fails. It includes a wall distance equation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, v2-f (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowv2f", "geom1")

parameters.name: TurbulenceModel
parameters.description: v2f; constants C_mu_v2f, C_tau, C_eta, C_L, C1, C2, Ceps1_v2f, Ceps2_v2f.

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Automatic or Low Re.

parameters.name: Inlet turbulence
parameters.description: Inlet needs k, ε and ζ (or intensity and length scale).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Less robust than k-ε; converge a k-ε or SST solution first and use it as the initial guess.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, Wilcox R-ω (spf)
tools.description: Reynolds-stress model (RANS-RSM) solving six transport equations for the Reynolds stresses plus the specific dissipation rate ω (Wilcox stress-ω). It captures turbulence anisotropy, secondary flows in noncircular ducts, streamline curvature and system rotation that eddy-viscosity models miss. It is a low-Reynolds-number model resolving the wall layer and includes a wall distance equation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, Wilcox R-ω (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowWilcoxRSM", "geom1")

parameters.name: TurbulenceModelType
parameters.description: RANS_RSM with RSMTurbulenceModel = WilcoxRSM (other options SSGLRR, EBRSM).

parameters.name: RDiffusionModel
parameters.description: Reynolds-stress diffusion: SimpleDiffusion, DalyHarlow, HanjalicLaunder, MellorHerring or Lumley.

parameters.name: RSMWallTreatment
parameters.description: LowReynoldsNumber (only option).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Needs a fine near-wall mesh (y+ about 1) and a good initial guess (for example from SST). Fully developed inflow is not available for RSM models.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, SSG-LRR (spf)
tools.description: Seven-equation Reynolds-stress model blending the Speziale–Sarkar–Gatski pressure-strain model away from walls with the Launder–Reece–Rodi model near walls, closed with an ω equation. It predicts secondary flows, swirling jets and rotating-pipe flows markedly better than two-equation models. The model is low-Re and uses a wall distance equation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, SSG-LRR (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowSSGLRR", "geom1")

parameters.name: RSMTurbulenceModel
parameters.description: SSGLRR (TurbulenceModelType = RANS_RSM).

parameters.name: RDiffusionModel
parameters.description: Reynolds-stress diffusion model selection.

parameters.name: Inlet anisotropy
parameters.description: RSMAnisotropyOption on inlets: isotropic turbulence or specified anisotropy.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Typically 2-3 times more expensive than SST; use P1+P1 with a boundary-layer mesh.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, Elliptic Blending R-ε (spf)
tools.description: Manceau–Hanjalić elliptic-blending Reynolds-stress model: six Reynolds-stress equations plus ε and an elliptic equation for a blending variable that switches the pressure-strain term between near-wall and homogeneous forms. It is the most physically complete RSM in COMSOL for wall-bounded flows with rotation, curvature and heat transfer. Only anisotropic turbulent thermal conductivity models can be used with it in nonisothermal flow.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, Elliptic Blending R-ε (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowEBRSM", "geom1")

parameters.name: RSMTurbulenceModel
parameters.description: EBRSM; constants C_mu_EB, sigmak_EB, Ceps1_EB, C_L_EB, C_eta_EB.

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Low Reynolds number (wall layer resolved).

parameters.name: Heat transport model
parameters.description: In Nonisothermal Flow the Anisotropic turbulent thermal conductivity option is enforced.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (new in 6.x). Start from a converged SST solution; RSM models do not support fully developed flow inlets.

tools.name: LES RBVM (spf)
tools.description: Large eddy simulation using the residual-based variational multiscale method: the large 3D unsteady eddies are resolved by the mesh and the small-scale effect is modeled consistently from the equation residual, so the model also reproduces laminar and transitional flow. It is for 3D time-dependent analyses only and by default uses a Low Re (no-slip) wall treatment. Typical uses are bluff-body wakes, jets, natural-convection transition and aeroacoustic sources.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Large Eddy Simulation > LES RBVM (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "LESRBVM", "geom1")

parameters.name: LESModel
parameters.description: RBVM (other choices RBVMWV and Smagorinsky) with TurbulenceModelType = LES.

parameters.name: LESWallTreatment
parameters.description: LowReynoldsNumber (default, velocity Dirichlet) or Automatic (L-VEL based tangential stress, allows coarser wall meshes).

parameters.name: Consistent stabilization
parameters.description: useDynamicSubgridTimescale and limitTimeStepInStabilization options.

parameters.name: Inlet synthetic turbulence
parameters.description: Include synthetic turbulence on Velocity inlets to inject resolved fluctuations.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Mesh resolution decides accuracy; check spf.dt_CFL for the time step and average results with a Time Average dataset.

tools.name: LES RBVMWV (spf)
tools.description: Residual-based variational multiscale LES with viscosity: like LES RBVM but adds a residual-based eddy-viscosity term that enhances the Reynolds-stress dissipation, making the model more dissipative and robust on coarser meshes. The modeling remains consistent, so it vanishes for fully resolved flow and is also valid for laminar/transitional regions. Only 3D and time-dependent.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Large Eddy Simulation > LES RBVMWV (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "LESRBVMWV", "geom1")

parameters.name: LESModel
parameters.description: RBVMWV; model constant Cvisc (default 0.074) editable with Edit LES model parameters.

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Low Re (default) or Automatic.

parameters.name: Turbulent Prandtl number
parameters.description: In Nonisothermal Flow the extra diffusion appears in the energy equation scaled by a turbulent Prandtl number.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Prefer RBVMWV over RBVM if the solution shows node-to-node wiggles on an under-resolved mesh.

tools.name: LES Smagorinsky (spf)
tools.description: Classical Smagorinsky large eddy simulation in which the subgrid stresses are modeled with an eddy viscosity proportional to the filter width squared and the strain rate. The model is inconsistent (it does not vanish for a fully resolved flow), so it is best for fully turbulent flows away from transition. 3D time-dependent analyses only; porous media domains are not available.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Large Eddy Simulation > LES Smagorinsky (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "LESSmagorinsky", "geom1")

parameters.name: LESModel
parameters.description: Smagorinsky with Smagorinsky constant Cs (default 0.1).

parameters.name: LESWallTreatment
parameters.description: Low Re (default) or Automatic.

parameters.name: Include synthetic turbulence
parameters.description: Velocity-inlet option generating Fourier-mode fluctuations from k and ε.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Excessively dissipative in laminar or near-wall regions; RBVM variants are the recommended default.

tools.name: DES RBVM, Spalart–Allmaras (spf)
tools.description: Hybrid detached eddy simulation: the Spalart–Allmaras RANS model covers the attached boundary layers while the RBVM LES model resolves the large eddies in separated regions and wakes. This avoids the prohibitive near-wall resolution of wall-resolved LES at high Reynolds numbers (vehicles, landing gear, bluff bodies). It solves the Navier–Stokes, continuity and SA equations and is 3D time-dependent only.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Detached Eddy Simulation > DES RBVM, Spalart–Allmaras (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "DESRBVMSpalartAllmaras", "geom1")

parameters.name: TurbulenceModelType
parameters.description: DES with DESTurbulenceModel = SpalartAllmaras and LESModel = RBVM.

parameters.name: Cdes
parameters.description: DES constant scaling the switching length (default 1).

parameters.name: DESWallTreatment
parameters.description: Automatic (default) or LowReynoldsNumber.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Needs Wall Distance Initialization. Grid-induced separation can occur if the wall-parallel mesh is too fine inside the boundary layer.

tools.name: DES RBVMWV, Spalart–Allmaras (spf)
tools.description: Detached eddy simulation combining Spalart–Allmaras RANS near walls with the more dissipative RBVMWV LES model in the resolved regions. It is the robust choice for DES on moderately resolved meshes. Only for 3D transient studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Detached Eddy Simulation > DES RBVMWV, Spalart–Allmaras (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "DESRBVMWVSpalartAllmaras", "geom1")

parameters.name: LESModel
parameters.description: RBVMWV (Cvisc editable).

parameters.name: Cdes
parameters.description: DES switching constant.

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Automatic or Low Re for the RANS part.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Initialize from a steady Spalart–Allmaras RANS solution to shorten the transient startup.

tools.name: DES Smagorinsky, Spalart–Allmaras (spf)
tools.description: Detached eddy simulation using the Smagorinsky subgrid model in the LES region and Spalart–Allmaras RANS near walls. It is the classical DES formulation found in literature benchmarks. 3D time-dependent only.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Detached Eddy Simulation > DES Smagorinsky, Spalart–Allmaras (spf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("spf", "DESSmagorinskySpalartAllmaras", "geom1")

parameters.name: LESModel
parameters.description: Smagorinsky with constant Cs.

parameters.name: Cdes
parameters.description: DES constant.

parameters.name: DESWallTreatment
parameters.description: Automatic or Low Re.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. For comparison studies with published DES data; RBVM-based DES is usually more accurate at the same mesh.

tools.name: Synthetic Turbulence Inlet (LES/DES Inlet)
tools.description: Option of the Inlet node (Velocity condition) available when the turbulence model type is LES or DES: a fluctuating velocity u'(t) built from random Fourier modes with a modified von Kármán spectrum is added to the mean inflow. The spectrum is scaled from the inlet k and ε (or intensity and length scale) and fluctuations are correlated in time to mimic a physical turbulent time scale. It removes the need for a long precursor domain to trigger turbulence.
tools.usage: Laminar/LES interface > Inlet > Boundary Condition: Velocity > Include synthetic turbulence; Java property: feature("inl1").set("includeSyntheticTurb", "1")

parameters.name: includeSyntheticTurb
parameters.description: 1 enables the synthetic fluctuations (Velocity inlet only).

parameters.name: IT / LT
parameters.description: Turbulent intensity and length scale defining k0 and ε0 of the spectrum.

parameters.name: N
parameters.description: Number of Fourier modes (default 100).

parameters.name: useRandomSeed
parameters.description: Use a fixed seed for reproducible random angles.

tools.notes: The largest resolved wavenumber is set by the smallest inlet element size (boundary layer elements excluded), so refine the inlet mesh to resolve the injected eddies.

tools.name: Turbulence Model Type and Wall Treatment Settings (spf)
tools.description: Interface-level Turbulence section of every Single-Phase Flow interface, exposed in Java as prop("TurbulenceModelProperty"). It lets one switch a Laminar Flow interface to any RANS-EVM, RANS-RSM, LES or DES model, choose the wall treatment and edit model constants without rebuilding the model. The same property also holds the heat-transport turbulence model options used by Nonisothermal Flow.
tools.usage: Select the spf node > Physical Model/Turbulence section; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("spf").prop("TurbulenceModelProperty").set(name, value)

parameters.name: TurbulenceModelType
parameters.description: None | RANS | RANS_RSM | LES | DES.

parameters.name: TurbulenceModel
parameters.description: AlgebraicYplus | LVEL | keps | Rkeps | komega | SST | lowRekeps | SpalartAllmaras | v2f (RANS-EVM).

parameters.name: RSMTurbulenceModel / LESModel / DESTurbulenceModel
parameters.description: WilcoxRSM | SSGLRR | EBRSM; RBVM | RBVMWV | Smagorinsky; SpalartAllmaras.

parameters.name: WallTreatment
parameters.description: Automatic | LowReynoldsNumber (k-ε variants also offer Wall functions).

parameters.name: includeRotationCurvatureCorrection / includeTransitionModeling / includeSAS
parameters.description: Rotation-curvature correction, γ-Reθ transition model (SST) and scale-adaptive simulation (SST-SAS).

parameters.name: editTurbulenceModelParameters
parameters.description: Exposes the model constants (Ceps1, Ceps2, C_mu, sigmak, ...).

tools.notes: Property names and values verified against COMSOL 6.4. Changing the model this way keeps the interface tag spf and all boundary conditions; remember to add a Wall Distance Initialization step for models that need it.

tools.name: Transition Modeling, γ-Reθ (Turbulent Flow, SST)
tools.description: Optional laminar-to-turbulent transition model for the SST interface: two extra transport equations for intermittency γ and transition-onset momentum-thickness Reynolds number Reθ predict natural and bypass transition on airfoils, turbine blades and low-Re external flows. When active, inlets and fans also ask for the intermittency. Without it, SST assumes fully turbulent boundary layers.
tools.usage: Turbulent Flow, SST (spf) > Turbulence > Include transition modeling; Java: physics("spf").prop("TurbulenceModelProperty").set("includeTransitionModeling", "1")

parameters.name: includeTransitionModeling
parameters.description: 1 activates the γ-Reθ equations.

parameters.name: gamma0
parameters.description: Inlet intermittency (Inlet/Fan turbulence conditions).

parameters.name: Model constants
parameters.description: C_TU1..3, C_PG1..3, Re_thetac_lim, C_SEP, ... when turbulence model parameters are edited.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Needs a low-Re boundary-layer mesh (y+ about 1) and a realistic free-stream turbulence intensity at the inlet; results are very sensitive to IT.

tools.name: Rotation-Curvature Correction (RANS-EVM)
tools.description: Correction for eddy-viscosity models (realizable k-ε, low-Re k-ε, k-ω, SST, ...) that multiplies the production terms by a factor based on the advection of the strain-rate tensor, sensitizing the model to system rotation and streamline curvature. It improves predictions in cyclones, swirling pipes, curved ducts and turbomachinery, and accounts for rotation from Rotating Frame or Frozen Rotor.
tools.usage: Turbulent Flow interface > Turbulence > Include rotation-curvature correction; Java: prop("TurbulenceModelProperty").set("includeRotationCurvatureCorrection", "1")

parameters.name: includeRotationCurvatureCorrection
parameters.description: 0 (default) or 1.

parameters.name: Model constants
parameters.description: c_r1, c_r2, c_r3 editable with Edit turbulence model parameters.

tools.notes: Adds nonlinearity; converge without the correction first. RSM models capture these effects inherently.

tools.name: Buoyancy-Induced Turbulence (Turbulent Flow)
tools.description: Option that adds buoyancy production/destruction terms to the turbulence transport equations when gravity is included, so that stable stratification damps and unstable stratification enhances turbulence. It matters for natural and mixed convection, atmospheric flows, fires and ventilation with large temperature differences. The contribution uses a turbulent Schmidt number ScT.
tools.usage: Turbulent Flow interface > Physical Model > Include gravity + Buoyancy-induced turbulence; Java: prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set("BuoyancyInducedTurbulence", "1")

parameters.name: IncludeGravity
parameters.description: Must be 1 (adds the Gravity global node).

parameters.name: BuoyancyInducedTurbulence
parameters.description: 1 to add buoyancy terms.

parameters.name: buoyancyContribution / ScT
parameters.description: Automatic or user-defined contribution; turbulent Schmidt number (default 1).

tools.notes: Normally combined with a Nonisothermal Flow coupling so that the density depends on temperature. See Application Library CFD_Module/Nonisothermal_Flow/displacement_ventilation.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow in Porous Media Domains (spf)
tools.description: With Enable porous media domains selected, turbulent flow interfaces can contain Fluid and Matrix Properties domains where the RANS equations become Brinkman-type equations with Darcy and Forchheimer drag, and turbulence is damped by additional source terms. This couples free turbulent flow and porous regions (filters, packed beds, heat exchangers, vegetation) in one interface. Porous Interface or Porous slip wall options handle the free/porous boundary.
tools.usage: Turbulent Flow interface > Physical Model > Enable porous media domains; then add Fluid and Matrix Properties on porous domains; Java: prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set("EnablePorousMediaDomains", "1")

parameters.name: EnablePorousMediaDomains
parameters.description: 1 adds porous domain features (FluidAndMatrixProperties, Forchheimer Drag, Mass Source).

parameters.name: PorousWallTreatment
parameters.description: PorousSlip (default) or PorousResolvedWall for walls adjacent to porous domains.

parameters.name: Porosity / permeability
parameters.description: Given in the Fluid and Matrix Properties node (usually from a Porous Material).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module plus a porous-flow-capable module license for the porous features.

tools.name: Inlet Turbulence Intensity and Length Scale (Turbulent Flow)
tools.description: Turbulence Conditions section of turbulent Inlet, Open Boundary, Grille and Boundary Stress nodes. Either turbulent intensity I_T and length scale L_T are given (from which k, ε, ω and the other variables are derived) or the turbulence variables are specified directly. Predefined intensity levels and a geometry-based length scale make it easy to set realistic inflow turbulence.
tools.usage: Turbulent Flow > Inlet > Turbulence Conditions; Java properties RANSVarOption, IT_list, IT, LT_list, LT, k0, ep0, om0

parameters.name: RANSVarOption
parameters.description: SpecifyTurbulentLengthScaleAndIntensity (default) or SpecifyTurbulenceVariables.

parameters.name: IT_list
parameters.description: low_turbulent_intensity (0.01) | lower_end_fully_turbulent (0.05, default) | upper_end_fully_turbulent (0.1) | user_defined.

parameters.name: LT_list
parameters.description: geometry_based (default) or user_defined length scale LT.

parameters.name: RANSAnisotropyOption
parameters.description: Isotropic turbulence or specified anisotropy (RSM models).

tools.notes: A common estimate for pipe inflow is L_T = 0.07 D. Fully developed flow inlets compute consistent turbulence variables automatically (not for RSM).

tools.name: Generate New Turbulence Model Interface (spf)
tools.description: Global feature that creates a copy of the current laminar or turbulent flow interface with a different turbulence model, inheriting all boundary conditions and settings except the initial values. It can also create a matching study whose initial values come from the solution of the original interface, which is the standard way to converge a demanding model (SST, v2-f, RSM) from a cheap one (Algebraic yPlus, k-ε).
tools.usage: Right-click the flow interface > Generate New Turbulence Model Interface, choose the model and click Create; Java: physics("spf").create("nturb1", "NewTurbulenceModel", -1)

parameters.name: Copy only active settings
parameters.description: Default on; disabled features are not transferred.

parameters.name: Turbulence model interface
parameters.description: k-ε, Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, k-ω, SST, Low Re k-ε, Spalart–Allmaras, v2-f, Wilcox R-ω, SSG-LRR.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Create a new study using the old solution as initial values.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Expressions referencing the old interface tag (for example spf.U in a Global Equation) must be updated manually in the generated interface.

tools.name: Incompressible Potential Flow (ipf)
tools.description: Solves the Laplace equation for a velocity potential of irrotational, inviscid, incompressible flow, giving velocity and (through Bernoulli) static pressure. Its main purpose is to provide cheap, well-behaved initial velocity fields for turbulent RANS, LES and DES simulations of external aerodynamics. Stationary analyses only.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Potential Flow > Incompressible Potential Flow (ipf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ipf", "IncompressiblePotentialFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Total pressure
parameters.description: Reference total pressure used to compute static pressure from the potential.

parameters.name: Velocity (velbc)
parameters.description: Boundary node prescribing normal velocity at inflow/outflow.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid Properties (fp1), Initial Values, Wall (wallbc1), Flow Continuity.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (also Microfluidics and Polymer Flow). Map its solution into the turbulent study with Values of Dependent Variables > Initial values: Solution.

tools.name: Potential Point Constraint (Incompressible Potential Flow)
tools.description: Point constraint fixing the value of the velocity potential at one point, which removes the null space of the pure-Neumann Laplace problem when no boundary prescribes the potential. It plays the same role as the Pressure Point Constraint in Navier–Stokes models.
tools.usage: Incompressible Potential Flow > Points > Potential Point Constraint; Java: physics("ipf").create("ppc1", "PotentialPointConstraint", 0)

parameters.name: Velocity potential
parameters.description: Value of φ at the selected point (usually 0).

tools.notes: Needed only when all boundaries use Wall/Velocity (flux) conditions.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, Laminar (hmnf)
tools.description: Predefined fully compressible flow interface solving mass, momentum and total energy for an ideal gas with Laminar Flow and Heat Transfer combined, valid for transonic and supersonic laminar flows (often at low pressure). It also supports heat transfer in solids and surface-to-surface radiation. Default nodes are Fluid, Wall, Thermal Insulation and Initial Values.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > High Mach Number Flow, Laminar (hmnf); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Reference temperature
parameters.description: Defines the zero of enthalpy; Include kinetic energy solves the conservative total-energy equation.

parameters.name: Turbulence model type
parameters.description: None by default; RANS-EVM or RANS-RSM converts it to a turbulent variant.

parameters.name: Dependent variables
parameters.description: u, p, T.

parameters.name: Pseudo time stepping
parameters.description: On by default for stationary high-Mach solves (CFL ramping).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Shocks need mesh refinement or adaptive meshing; use P1 elements and the default consistent stabilization.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, k-ε (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible RANS interface for turbulent transonic/supersonic flow with the standard k-epsilon model and wall functions, solving continuity, momentum, energy (ideal gas) and k, ε. It is robust for nozzle, ejector and jet flows where boundary-layer details are secondary. Default Fluid node uses Sutherland's law for viscosity and conductivity.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > High Mach Number Flow, k-ε (hmnf); Java: physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentkeps", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Wall functions (default) or automatic.

parameters.name: Inlet flow condition
parameters.description: Characteristics based, Supersonic or Subsonic (HighMachNumberFlowInlet).

parameters.name: Outlet flow condition
parameters.description: Hybrid, Supersonic or Subsonic.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, Spalart–Allmaras (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible RANS with the one-equation Spalart–Allmaras model, the standard for external transonic aerodynamics (wings, airfoils, diffusers with shock-induced separation). It resolves the boundary layer to the wall and needs a Wall Distance Initialization study step.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > High Mach Number Flow, Spalart–Allmaras (hmnf); Java: physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentSpalartAllmaras", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Automatic or Low Re.

parameters.name: Inlet
parameters.description: Mach number, static or total pressure/temperature and flow direction.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Stationary with Initialization (Wall Distance Initialization + Stationary).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, SST (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible RANS interface with Menter's SST model, combining accurate near-wall k-ω behavior with free-stream independence; recommended for shock/boundary-layer interaction and separated supersonic flows. Includes a wall distance equation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > High Mach Number Flow, SST (hmnf); Java: physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentSST", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Automatic (default) or Low Re.

parameters.name: Transition / rotation-curvature options
parameters.description: Available as for incompressible SST.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid (fluid1), Wall, Thermal Insulation, Gravity, Rotating Frame, Initial Values.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, k-ω (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible RANS interface with the Wilcox revised k-omega model, suitable for wall-bounded supersonic and transonic flows with adverse pressure gradients. Automatic wall treatment is the default.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > High Mach Number Flow, k-ω (hmnf); Java: physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentkomega", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Automatic or Low Re.

parameters.name: Inlet turbulence
parameters.description: Intensity and length scale or k and ω.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. More sensitive to free-stream ω than SST.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, Low Re k-ε (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible RANS interface with the AKN low-Reynolds k-epsilon model that resolves the near-wall region; used for jets and nozzles where both the wall layer and free shear layers matter. Includes wall distance.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > High Mach Number Flow, Low Reynolds Number k-ε (hmnf); Java: physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentLowRekeps", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Automatic or Low Re.

parameters.name: Outlet
parameters.description: Hybrid outlet supports both sub- and supersonic exits.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, Algebraic yPlus and L-VEL (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible flow interfaces using the algebraic Algebraic yPlus or L-VEL turbulence models, which need no turbulence transport equations. They are the most robust choice for getting a first compressible turbulent solution, for example as an initial guess for SST or Spalart–Allmaras runs.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > ... Algebraic yPlus / L-VEL; Java: physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentAlgebraicYplus", "geom1") or "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentLVEL"

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: AlgebraicYplus or LVEL.

parameters.name: Wall distance
parameters.description: Wall Distance Initialization needed.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, Realizable k-ε and v2-f (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible turbulent flow interfaces with the realizable k-epsilon (wall functions) or the v2-f (low-Re, anisotropy-aware) model. They extend the compressible toolset to jets, swirl and heat-transfer-dominated high-speed flows.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > ... Realizable k-ε / v2-f; Java: physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentRkeps", "geom1") or "HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentv2f"

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: Rkeps or v2f.

parameters.name: Rotation-curvature correction
parameters.description: Optional for realizable k-ε.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow, Reynolds-Stress Models (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible RANS-RSM interfaces: Wilcox R-ω, SSG-LRR and Elliptic Blending R-ε solve transport equations for all Reynolds stresses together with energy for an ideal gas. They are intended for high-speed flows with strong anisotropy such as swirling combustor inlets, curved supersonic ducts and turbomachinery passages.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > ... Wilcox R-ω / SSG-LRR / Elliptic Blending R-ε; Java type ids: HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentWilcoxRSM, HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentSSGLRR, HighMachNumberFlowTurbulentEBRSM

parameters.name: RSMTurbulenceModel
parameters.description: WilcoxRSM, SSGLRR or EBRSM.

parameters.name: Heat transport
parameters.description: Anisotropic turbulent thermal conductivity available with RSM models.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Start from a converged SST solution.

tools.name: Fluid (High Mach Number Flow)
tools.description: Default domain node of the High Mach Number Flow interfaces adding continuity, momentum and temperature equations for an ideal gas, including viscous heating and pressure work by default. Thermal conductivity and dynamic viscosity default to Sutherland's law, and the thermodynamics are defined by a specific gas constant or mean molar mass plus Cp or γ.
tools.usage: High Mach Number Flow > Fluid (fluid1); Java type HighMachNumberFlowModel: physics("hmnf").feature("fluid1")

parameters.name: Thermal conductivity k
parameters.description: Sutherland's law (k_ref, T_k,ref, S_k), From material or User defined.

parameters.name: Dynamic viscosity μ
parameters.description: Sutherland's law (default), From material or User defined.

parameters.name: Gas constant type
parameters.description: Specific gas constant R_s or Mean molar mass M_n.

parameters.name: Specify Cp or γ
parameters.description: Heat capacity at constant pressure or ratio of specific heats.

tools.example:
// GUI: High Mach Number Flow > Fluid 1 > Dynamic viscosity: Sutherland's law (air: mu_ref 1.716e-5 Pa*s, T_ref 273 K, S 111 K)
model.component("comp1").physics("hmnf").feature("fluid1");
tools.notes: Only ideal gases are supported; volume forces and heat sources are separate nodes.

tools.name: Inlet (High Mach Number Flow)
tools.description: Compressible inlet using the flow characteristics to decide how many quantities to impose: Characteristics based (default) handles both subsonic and supersonic inflow from Mach number, static or total pressure/temperature and flow direction. Supersonic imposes all state variables, Subsonic prescribes velocity or pressure plus temperature or heat flux.
tools.usage: High Mach Number Flow > Inlet; Java: physics("hmnf").create("inl1", "HighMachNumberFlowInlet", 2)

parameters.name: FlowCondition
parameters.description: CharacteristicsBased | Supersonic | Subsonic.

parameters.name: InputState
parameters.description: StaticConditions (p0stat, T0stat) or TotalConditions (p0tot, T0tot).

parameters.name: Ma0
parameters.description: Inlet Mach number (default 1.5).

parameters.name: FlowDirection
parameters.description: NormalInflow or userDefined with direction nM.

tools.notes: Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4. Consistent inlet/outlet conditions (see theory) avoid over-specification at subsonic boundaries.

tools.name: Outlet (High Mach Number Flow)
tools.description: Compressible outlet whose Hybrid condition (default) enforces the given static or total pressure only where the local outflow is subsonic and extrapolates everything where it is supersonic. Supersonic and Subsonic options fix the behavior when the outflow regime is known; the subsonic variant offers normal stress or pressure with optional backflow suppression.
tools.usage: High Mach Number Flow > Outlet; Java: physics("hmnf").create("out1", "HighMachNumberFlowOutlet", 2)

parameters.name: FlowCondition
parameters.description: HybridOutlet | Supersonic | Subsonic.

parameters.name: InputState
parameters.description: Static (p0stat) or Total (p0tot) pressure for the hybrid outlet.

parameters.name: BoundaryCondition (subsonic)
parameters.description: NormalStress (f0) or Pressure (p0), SuppressBackflow.

tools.notes: Place outlets far enough downstream that shocks do not intersect them.

tools.name: Compressible Euler Equations (cee)
tools.description: Time-explicit discontinuous Galerkin (dG-FEM) solver for the inviscid compressible Euler equations with density, momentum and total energy as dependent variables. Shock capturing and positivity-preserving limiters make it suitable for blast waves, shock tubes and transient transonic/supersonic flows; the method is very memory lean. Simulations are always time dependent.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > Compressible Euler Equations (cee); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cee", "CompressibleEulerEquationsTimeExplicit", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid Properties
parameters.description: Ideal-gas constants (gas constant and γ).

parameters.name: Inlet / Outlet / Wall / Symmetry
parameters.description: Characteristic boundary conditions (InletBoundary, OutletBoundary, WallBC).

parameters.name: Volume Force / Heat Source / Gravity
parameters.description: Optional source nodes.

parameters.name: Discretization order
parameters.description: dG shape-function order; time step from the CFL condition.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. The time-explicit dG solver is not compatible with Moving Mesh or Deformed Geometry that changes during time stepping.
